Cognize

KOG-nyze · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To cognize to become aware of, perceive, or come to know something through mental effort.

It took the jury several long minutes to fully cognize the significance of the forensic report the lawyer had just read aloud.

Worked Example

Long before he could speak in full sentences, the toddler could already cognize the difference between his mother's footsteps and a stranger's.

Cognizing something doesn't require language at all -- it's the basic mental act of perceiving and registering that something is true or present.

How Cognize Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

perceive

perceive: to become aware of through the senses or mind

apprehend

apprehend: to grasp something mentally; to come to understand it

Antonyms

overlook

overlook: to fail to notice or register something

disregard

disregard: to choose not to think about or consider something

How Strong Is It? — notice → cognize → comprehend

notice vs. cognize

notice vs. cognize: To notice something is simply to register that it exists, a much lighter mental action than fully cognizing it.

comprehend vs. cognize

comprehend vs. cognize: To comprehend something is to understand it completely and deeply, a fuller mental grasp than simply cognizing it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — co-

prefix — co-: together, thoroughly (an intensifying prefix) (Latin)

root — gnize

root — gnize: to know (Latin gnoscere, 'to know')

Put it together

Put it together: Cognize combines co- ('together,' an intensifying prefix) with gnize (from Latin gnoscere, 'to know') -- literally 'to come to know fully,' which is exactly what cognize means: to become aware of or mentally grasp something.

Use the root in a new word: recognize

Use the root in a new word: recognize: She immediately recognized her old teacher's voice across the crowded reunion hall.
